cards.explanation: The answer is that they gain property and grow greatly in number. The Israelites settled in Goshen, "…acquired property there and became fruitful and increased greatly in number." (Genesis 47:27) Property and a growing family, all in one verse, friends. I've had batches that rose less than that.

The answer is that Jacob wants to be buried with his fathers outside Egypt. He says, "Do not bury me in Egypt, but when I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me with them." (Genesis 47:29-30) He wants to rest with his family, not in the land where he's spent his last seventeen years. That's a big ask, and he's asking his son.

The answer is False. Joseph says, "I will do as you have requested." and that's a solid answer. (Genesis 47:30) Jacob still comes back with, "Swear to me…" (Genesis 47:31) So Joseph swears, and his word gets put on the record twice, friends.

The answer is True. After Joseph swears, the text says "…Israel bowed in worship at the head of his bed." (Genesis 47:31) He's weak, and he's still worshiping, friends. I'd call that a man who knows who to turn to.

The answer is False. The text says "Israel rallied his strength and sat up in bed." (Genesis 48:2) His father is ill, but he sits up for Joseph anyway, friends. Somebody pulled himself together for this visit.

The word is "descendants." God told Jacob He would give the land "…to your descendants after you as an everlasting possession." (Genesis 48:4) The promise reaches to the family that comes after him. And look at that word, everlasting, friends. That's a long time to hold a deed.

The answer is that they will be counted as Jacob's own sons. Jacob says Joseph's two sons born in Egypt "…shall be reckoned as mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine…" (Genesis 48:5) He's taking his grandsons in as his own. That's a promotion nobody saw coming, friends.

The answer is True. Jacob says, "Any children born to you after them shall be yours…" (Genesis 48:6) So Ephraim and Manasseh get counted as Jacob's, and later children stay Joseph's, friends. They'd be called by the names of their brothers in the territory they inherit.

The answer is beside the road to Ephrath. Jacob says, "…I buried her there beside the road to Ephrath…" and the text adds, in parentheses, that Ephrath is Bethlehem. (Genesis 48:7) Jacob says Rachel died to his sorrow, so I think this memory still weighs on him, friends.
The answer is True. The text says "…Israel’s eyesight was poor because of old age; he could hardly see." (Genesis 48:10) That detail matters later in the story, friends. Hold onto it.

The word is "children." Israel says, "I never expected to see your face again, but now God has let me see your children as well." (Genesis 48:11) He gets Joseph back, and then a bonus, friends. I think that's a very full heart.

The answer is that he crosses his hands and puts his right on Ephraim. Israel "…stretched out his right hand and put it on the head of Ephraim, the younger; and crossing his hands, he put his left on Manasseh’s head…" (Genesis 48:14) Manasseh was the firstborn, and Joseph had lined things up carefully, friends. Israel crossed his hands anyway.

The answer is True. Israel says, "…may they be called by my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they grow into a multitude upon the earth." (Genesis 48:16) He asks for his name and the names of Abraham and Isaac to be on those boys, friends. My name is carved on a handle, and I'm proud of it, but that is a whole other level of name.

The answer is that Joseph tells him this one is the firstborn, so put his right hand on him. Joseph says, "Not so, my father! This one is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head." (Genesis 48:18) Manasseh is the firstborn, so Joseph speaks up for him, friends. I think he figures his dad just made a mistake.
The answer is False. The text says "…his father refused." (Genesis 48:19) Israel keeps his right hand on Ephraim, friends. Joseph pushes, and his father doesn't budge.

The answer is that Ephraim will be greater and his offspring will become many nations. Israel says Manasseh "…shall become a people, and he too shall be great; nevertheless, his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall become a multitude of nations." (Genesis 48:19) Manasseh gets a real blessing too, friends. Ephraim's is just bigger.

The answer is True. Israel says, "Look, I am about to die, but God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers." (Genesis 48:21) He knows his time is short, friends. And he points Joseph to what God will do.

The answer is a ridge of land. Israel says, "…I give the ridge of land that I took from the Amorites with my sword and bow." (Genesis 48:22) He gives it to Joseph as one who is above his brothers, friends. That's a gift worth getting from your dad.
